summary.name: Monzo Response
summary.one_liner: Monzo's engineering blog post describing how it handles incidents, and Response, the open-source Slack-based (ChatOps) incident tool built to support that process.
use_cases: Coordinating a live production outage in Slack
Escalating an incident to other on-call teams quickly
Setting and tracking incident severity and lead
Updating a public status page during customer-impacting incidents
Logging follow-up actions during an incident
Prompting engineers to complete post-incident reports
summary.what_it_does: The page explains Monzo's incident response process, covering internal and customer communication, defined incident roles (an incident lead), and escalation to on-call engineers. Monzo built Response, a Slack bot driven by commands such as /incident, which creates an incident post, a dedicated channel, and a live incident document. The tool can page on-call engineers via PagerDuty, escalate to specialist teams with a spoken message, update the status page, and log follow-up actions. It also sets severity reminders every 15 minutes and automatically notifies the regulator comms team for serious issues, and it reminds the incident lead to complete the report afterwards.
notable: ChatOps-based incident coordination inside Slack using slash and @incident commands
Automatic severity prompts every 15 minutes until a severity is set
Escalation to other on-call teams via paging with a custom spoken message
caveats: Tool is tied to Slack and PagerDuty integrations, which the page names as Monzo's own stack
Page describes Monzo's internal process; it is a blog post, not a product landing page
